note: Real LLaDA-V forward passes (fp16, Apple M4 Pro GPU via PyTorch MPS) on real Wikimedia Commons photos. Baseline = always look: each step one full image-conditioned pass unmasks the single highest-confidence masked position with its argmax; at every step a cheap text-only pass (LOWN style: visual rows removed, original absolute positions kept) is run on the same partially unmasked canvas. Both distributions are recorded. lown = replay of the LOWN rule on this baseline trajectory (memory = full prediction from the last look; trust when the cheap argmax at the chosen position equals the memory argmax, else look and refresh); the canvas is the baseline's at every step, so it is a counterfactual replay, not a separate LOWN decode. Image preprocessing uses LLaDA-V's anyres path restricted to a single 384x384 grid (base view + 1 tile, ~1.4k visual tokens) to fit memory and time; the paper uses up to anyres_max_4. Tokens 126080/126081/126346/126347 suppressed as in LOWN's lown.py; decoding stops at the first committed <|eot_id|> (positions after it are dropped), as in LOWN. Logits computed for answer positions only, softmax in float32 (MPS has no float64). Because 16.9 GB of fp16 weights did not fit beside the machine's existing wired memory, decoder layers and the LM head were streamed from disk one layer at a time; ms_full / ms_cheap are GPU compute times with the layer resident (synchronised per layer, weight transfer excluded), median over steps; ms_step_wall includes streaming. Probabilities are rounded to 4 decimals. Not the authors' setup; numbers are from this run only.
